On paper it's a representative democracy, but in practice incentives—gerrymandering, barriers to voting, outsized money/media influence, and institutional capture—skew who actually gets represented. That said, these are largely structural problems that practical, bipartisan reforms can fix so future generations inherit a healthier system.

I lean against saying the U.S. is being governed democratically today. Elections and institutions exist, but concentrated money, powerful unelected agencies, platform/media gatekeeping, gerrymandering, and patchwork state rules routinely distort the popular will and weaken real accountability. From my work in media I see how narratives and incentives shape outcomes — until we fix transparency, incentives, and election administration, it’s hard to call our governance fully democratic.
